Inputs read: card #31112 body and all 16 comments (triage 6706617330, the slice 1 to 4 claims, reports and releases, the slice 5 claim 6731732071 and dev report 6731975880); PR #31791 body, file list and `git diff origin/main...pr/31791` at the head; the check-runs on the head. The dispatch order and the seat's conclusions were not inputs.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set: no runtime, schema or public-surface change. The diff adds ten os:check marks (SKILL.md 2, examples-flows.md 1, state-machines-and-approvals.md 2, integration-recipes.md 5), taking the skill from 3 to 13 of 19 fenced ts blocks, with one import line per block and a three-token wrapper on four of them. Right: every marker sits at column 0 on the line directly above a bare ts or typescript fence, which is what `FENCE_OPEN_RE` (checker line 711, anchored at column 0) and the adjacency rule (`marked`, checker line 632) require.
- Each newly marked block compiles for the right reason, not by widening or casting. Right: the types are the spec's own authoring halves and nothing else. `FlowNode` is `z.input of FlowNodeSchema` (flow.zod.ts:2009), exported by `@objectstack/spec/automation` (automation/index.ts:4). `StateMachineValidation` is `z.input of StateMachineValidationSchema` (validation.zod.ts:555), exported by `@objectstack/spec/data` (data/index.ts:228). `defineFlow`, `defineConnector` and `cel` are root exports (packages/spec/src/index.ts lines 131, 181, 281), so the five recipes' move from `@objectstack/spec/integration` to the root is a true statement about the surface. No `any`, no `as`, no widened literal anywhere in the ten blocks.
- Gate verdicts on the head: `Type Check · consumer gates` (lint.yml job at line 5966; it runs `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:skill-examples` at line 6270) concluded success, so the 13 marks compile against the built spec. `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates` (token ratchet, skill links), `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Type Check · workspace / source gates / debt ledger`, `Build Core`, `Live E2E UI` concluded success. `Test Core (1/8)` and `(2/8)` were still in progress when this record was written; the diff touches no path they judge.
- Token ratchet, audited by arithmetic on the tree (ceil of utf8 bytes over 4; SKILL.md's 20-byte stamp line excluded): SKILL.md 6527 to 6522 of 6527, examples-flows.md 1494 to 1490 of 1494, integration-recipes.md 2588 to 2591 of 2595, state-machines-and-approvals.md 5825 to 5809 of 5825. Matches the PR body's table; no ceiling moved (`scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` lines 561, 1121, 1194, 1236 unchanged). Right.
- The four stated deviations. (a) SKILL.md's two `script` blocks (lines 265 and 285) are fenced three spaces deep inside list item 3 of Valid-but-silently-wrong; `FENCE_OPEN_RE` reads column-0 fences only, so they cannot be marked without re-indenting the list. Right. (b) The fragment note is written once in state-machines-and-approvals.md (line 5) and nowhere else; the other three files close at 4 to 5 tokens of headroom. Right, and for SKILL.md a fragment note would be false anyway (its unmarked blocks are list-item fences, not fragments). (c) `FlowNode.config` is `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()).optional()` (flow.zod.ts, the `config` key of `flowNodeObject`), so the two SKILL.md marks and the node configs inside the three marked `defineFlow` blocks check the node envelope only. Right; see the nit in ④ for the same fact on `providerConfig`. (d) The state-machine block is typed `StateMachineValidation`, the union member, because the `ValidationRule` union gives no excess-key check on a `state_machine` literal. Right: `StateMachineValidationSchema` is a `strictObject` over `BASE_VALIDATION_SHAPE` plus `type`, `field`, `transitions`, `initialStates` (validation.zod.ts:187), and the dev's measured TS2561 on a planted `initialState` is the behaviour that member gives.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/31112-automation-skill-examples-checked.md`: `'@objectstack/skills': patch` (the package exists at `packages/skills/package.json`), `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, matching the PR body. The diff publishes prose in the skill bundle and nothing else: no spec export, schema key or route changes, so no narrowing and no feature. Patch is the right level and `Clause-②: no` is the right line. The body's one-paragraph summary of the changeset names the same ten blocks the diff marks.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags (report 6731975880 and the PR body's Acceptance notes), each answered:
- `check:skill-examples` is not in the derived gate list for a `skills/**` diff and was run by hand. Answered: it is CI's `Type Check · consumer gates` job, green on the head.
- Two SKILL.md `script` blocks left unmarked (indented fences). Answered right in ①(a); an accepted deviation, no action.
- Fragment note paid only in state-machines-and-approvals.md. Answered right in ①(b); an accepted deviation.
- `FlowNode.config` is a record, so the SKILL.md marks check the envelope only. Answered right in ①(c); the same holds for `providerConfig` on the five connector recipes (④ nit 2).
- No ceiling raised or lowered. Answered by arithmetic in ①.
- Built on the default tier under the no-Fable-build exit. This record is the lane's isolated contract review on the mandated tier.
- Observation, not filed: the `ValidationRule` union type does not refuse an unknown key on a `state_machine` literal while runtime parsing does. Out of this PR's scope; a TypeScript-only gap with no runtime effect. Left unfiled is acceptable; the seat may open a follow-up card on `packages/spec/src/data/validation.zod.ts` if it wants the union to carry per-member excess-key checking.
- The dev's post-delivery flag that several cuts are pointers under the domain:skills lane ruling: judged cut by cut in ④.
No `open_questions` entry exists in the report; nothing to escalate.

### ④ Design judgment

Every `hits` file against the code it cites and the card's eval prompts (skills/objectstack-automation/evals/flows-triggers-approvals.json and integrations-declared.json):

- `SKILL.md`. The `notify` node (line 115) and the start node (line 395) typed `FlowNode`: `flowNodeObject` is a strict object whose keys include `id`, `type` (a string with the reserved-name regex, so `'notify'` and `'start'` pass), `label` and `config`; both blocks use exactly those keys, so the mark is honest about the envelope and the dev's planted `next` producing TS2353 is the expected refusal. The two blocks still carry every teaching the evals lean on (the 4th recipient form for a non-user applicant; `record-after-update` with a transition `condition`). Holds.
- `references/examples-flows.md`. The time-relative sweep wrapped in `defineFlow`: `FlowSchema` (flow.zod.ts:1084) requires `name`, `label`, `type` in the enum at line 1171 (`schedule` is a member), `nodes`, `edges`, and takes `runAs` at line 1230; the block supplies all of them, the start node's `timeRelative` sits under `config` as the schema places it, and an empty `edges` array is legal input. Holds.
- `references/state-machines-and-approvals.md`. The `state_machine` rule: `name` matches the snake_case regex, `message` is the one required base key and is present, `label` and `initialStates` are optional, `transitions` is a record of string arrays. Holds. The discount approval flow wrapped in `defineFlow` with `cel`: `record_change` is in the type enum; `cel` is a tagged template returning an `EvaluatedExpression` envelope (expression.zod.ts:490), which the edge `condition` and the start node's `config` accept; approval node configs are inside the record `config` and so unchecked by this mark, as ①(c) says. Holds.
- `references/integration-recipes.md`. Recipes 1 to 5 under `defineConnector` from the root: `ConnectorSchema` (connector.zod.ts:1308) takes `name` (snake_case regex), `label`, `type` (`'api'`), `provider`, `providerConfig` and `auth` as `ConnectorInstanceAuthSchema`; the `bearer`, `api-key` with `headerName`, and `basic` with `username` shapes in the blocks are the same shapes the spec's own fixtures use (connector-auth-static-kinds.test.ts:30 to 32), and the dev's planted top-level `authentication` producing TS2322 is the refusal the schema is built to give. The Stripe, legacy-ERP and DocuSign eval prompts still find their recipes (1, 5, and 4 plus 6) intact. Holds.

Every cut in the PR body's cut list, judged under the lane ruling (a pointer the agent follows to reach content, that is a cross-reference to another file, section, row or repository, is not payable; only a restatement whose substance survives where the agent reads anyway is payable):

1. SKILL.md, the state-introspection route cut from the State Machines pointer line. Restatement: the link to the file stays; the route survives at state-machines-and-approvals.md:49 (Introspection), the file the surviving link reaches. Payable.
2. SKILL.md, "write them right the first time". No rule. Payable.
3. SKILL.md, the "start node alone, not a whole flow" sentence shortened. Restatement; the list of flow-owned keys is the same list as before (it omitted `name` on main too, see nit 3). Payable.
4. SKILL.md, "(see Inbound webhook triggers below)" shortened to "(Inbound webhook triggers)". The cross-reference itself (the section name) survives; only "see" and "below" went. Payable.
5. SKILL.md, "section Time-relative triggers, scheduled per-record date sweep" shortened to the section name. The file-and-section pointer survives; the cut tail is a restatement of the Flow Types `schedule` row at SKILL.md:44. Payable.
6. examples-flows.md, "(moved verbatim from SKILL.md)" cut from the title. A provenance stub of the kind card item 2 removes. Payable.
7. examples-flows.md, the sweep's "a sweep has no trigger user, elevate explicitly" comment. Restatement; it survives on the first example's `runAs: 'system'` at line 23 of the same file. Payable.
8. state-machines-and-approvals.md, Branching bullet "Send back for revision (ADR-0044), see Send-back for revision above". A cross-reference to a section, and the only entry that lists send-back among the reject routings. Pointer. NOT payable (about 20 tokens). Paid for: the approval-flow block's mark.
9. state-machines-and-approvals.md, "See the showcase_budget_approval flow in the showcase app in the framework repo for the canonical shape". A cross-reference to a repository, and the only route to a complete send-back flow: this file holds a node-and-edge excerpt only (the unmarked fragment under Three pieces author it). Pointer. NOT payable (about 27 tokens). Paid for: the `state_machine` rule's mark.
10. state-machines-and-approvals.md, "(the shipped showcase_dynamic_approval flow in the showcase app is this shape)". A cross-reference to a repository. Pointer under the ruling's form test. NOT payable (about 20 tokens). Paid for: the `state_machine` rule's mark and the fragment note. Note for the seat: the shape it names is the complete marked block that follows it, so what the agent loses is the name of a shipped instance, not the shape; if the seat reads the ruling by its rationale this one is a provenance restatement.
11. state-machines-and-approvals.md, "(SKILL.md section Trigger Configuration)" cut from the approval flow's start-node comment. A cross-reference to a SKILL.md section. Pointer under the ruling's form test. NOT payable (about 9 tokens). Paid for: the approval-flow block's own mark (the cut is inside that block). Note for the seat: the content it points at is the start node directly under the comment and SKILL.md is the skill's root file.
12. integration-recipes.md, "The rule is SKILL.md section Integrations are declared, not coded; this file is the shapes". A cross-reference to the SKILL.md section that owns the rule; an agent entering this file from the references index has no other way back to it. Pointer. NOT payable (about 22 tokens). Paid for: recipe 1's mark.
13. integration-recipes.md, "(SKILL.md's connector_action row)". A cross-reference to a table row. Pointer under the ruling's form test. NOT payable (about 10 tokens). Paid for: recipe 2's mark. Note for the seat: the row's substance (a value-slot map; a top-level CEL envelope is evaluated, other values kept as written) is restated at the cut site.
14. integration-recipes.md, the import-path bullet shortened to "defineConnector and defineFlow register in defineStack". Restatement; the import paths now sit, compiled, on the first line of each of the five marked blocks. Payable.
15. integration-recipes.md, recipe 3's "To let an agent run the sweep on request: objectstack-ai section Actions as AI Tools" comment. A cross-reference to another skill's section; the content (an Action of type `flow` exposed as an AI tool, skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md:135) exists only there. Pointer. NOT payable (about 21 tokens). Paid for: recipe 3's mark.
16. integration-recipes.md, recipe 4's "The sender signs each post under CARRIER_HOOK_SECRET (SKILL.md Signature bullet)". A cross-reference to the Signature bullet (SKILL.md:372) together with the fact that the default scheme signs under the start node's `secretRef`; SKILL.md:372 points forward to recipe 4 ("Vendor-signed: config.signature replaces it (recipe 4)") and recipe 4 now points nowhere back. Pointer. NOT payable (about 22 tokens). Paid for: recipe 4's mark.

Findings:

- should-fix (F1): eight cuts are pointers and unpayable under the lane ruling: cuts 8, 9, 10, 11 in state-machines-and-approvals.md and cuts 12, 13, 15, 16 in integration-recipes.md. Restore each pointer. The budgets then do not close: state-machines-and-approvals.md has 16 tokens of headroom and the four pointers cost about 76, so about 60 tokens must come out; its two new marks and the fragment note cost about 60 (state_machine rule about 32, approval flow about 21, note about 8), so with no other restatement to cut, unmark both blocks and drop the note, or find about 60 tokens of restatement in the file. integration-recipes.md has 4 tokens of headroom and the four pointers cost about 74, so about 70 must come out; its marks cost about 21 (recipe 1), 18 (recipes 2, 3, 5 each) and 17 (recipe 4), so unmark recipes 1 to 4 (about 73) and keep recipe 5, or find the tokens in restatement. SKILL.md and examples-flows.md have no pointer cut and keep their marks. If the seat rules cuts 10, 11 and 13 restatements by the ruling's rationale (the pointed-at content is at the cut site), the unpayable set is 8, 9, 12, 15, 16 (about 112 tokens) and the state-machines budget needs about 31 tokens (unmark the state_machine rule), while integration-recipes still needs about 61 (unmark recipes 1 to 3 or 1, 2 and 4).
- nit (N1): the PR body's Acceptance note says `FlowNode.config` is a record so SKILL.md's marks check the envelope only, and says nothing of `providerConfig`, which is also `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` (connector.zod.ts:1036); the five recipe marks check the connector envelope and the `auth` variant, not `spec`, `baseUrl`, `transport` or `include`. PR-body prose only; no tree effect. A one-line addition on the body, or left as is.
- nit (N2): SKILL.md:390 lists the keys a flow owns as `label`, `type`, `nodes`, `edges` and omits `name`, which `FlowSchema` requires (flow.zod.ts:1131). Pre-existing on main and unchanged by this PR; a follow-up or the next SKILL.md edit.

No must-fix. The should-fix F1 earns a delta review of its fix.
